messages.user: Can you explain the word order of the first part? Can I say "Wenn jemand entdeckt mich" instead?

In German, when a subordinate clause begins with "wenn" (if/when), the conjugated verb goes to the end of the clause. The standard word order is: conjunction + object (accusative) + subject + verb. So "Wenn mich jemand entdeckt" is correct: "wenn" + "mich" (object) + "jemand" (subject) + "entdeckt" (verb at the end).

You cannot say "Wenn jemand entdeckt mich" because that uses main clause word order (subject-verb-object), which is incorrect in a subordinate clause. Subordinate clauses require the verb to be placed at the end.
